mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1.5% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate signals collapsing consumer demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM < -1.5% AND UNRATE rises MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by more than 1.5% month-over-month and UNRATE rises simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the participation rate (implied by stable PAYEMS and rising UNRATE) above 66% for three consecutive months suggests a tighter labor market, which supports wage growth and boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS stable while participation implied > 66%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when implied participation exceeds 66% for three consecutive months with stable PAYEMS and rising UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.
